name: TESSERA BioOps Lab Technician Coverall
description:
Issued to TESSERA's bench-level geneware technicians working in BSL-2 and BSL-3 environments, this full-body coverall is constructed from a microporous film laminate that blocks particulates, aerosolized biologicals, and most common chemical splashes. The exterior is TESSERA's clinical white with a subtle helix-pattern emboss visible only under UV — a mark of authenticity that prevents counterfeit uniforms from entering secure lab areas. Integrated hood and booties attach via sealed magnetic closures. Disposable in theory, but most techs wash and reuse them until the laminate integrity fails, typically at around 30 cycles.

The suit is designed with the full range of TESSERA's own geneware modifications in mind — there are discrete fin-shaped vents along the spine for bioluminescent skin that can overheat under sealed suits, and the hood has a structured internal frame to accommodate horn clearance up to 18cm. A wrist-mounted contamination sensor logs exposure events and syncs to the wearer's BCI. The suit does not accommodate external chrome augmentation well; workers with significant cyberware typically request custom-cut versions at additional cost, which TESSERA docks from their pay.
cultural_context: TESSERA lab techs are a complicated caste — educated enough to understand what they're working on, but paid just enough to keep them from leaving. The white coverall is a daily reminder of their position: visible, trackable, replaceable. Some techs decorate the inside lining where inspectors won't see.
story_hooks: A contamination sensor log from a discarded coverall shows a tech was exposed to a compound that doesn't appear in any TESSERA public research manifest.
Someone is selling used TESSERA coveralls on the gray market — still containing trace biologicals from the lab. Whether that's valuable or dangerous depends on who's buying.
A new hire discovers that the 'custom cut' surcharge for her chrome arm has been quietly added to her contract as permanent debt, not a one-time fee.

physical_description.visual_profile: A pristine clinical white full-body coverall that reads as institutional and sterile at first glance, but reveals subtle design intentionality on closer inspection. The silhouette is slightly relaxed to accommodate layered undergarments and various body modifications, with a structured hood that gives the wearer an almost helmet-like appearance when sealed. Projects authority and biomedical purpose in equal measure.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso and limbs to allow freedom of movement during detailed lab work; the waist has subtle gathering to prevent bunching. The hood fits snugly around the face but leaves generous internal volume for head modifications. Booties are roomy to slip over standard footwear. Overall impression: functional, not flattering.
physical_description.primary_material: Microporous film laminate composite — a technical nonwoven that appears smooth and slightly reflective under normal light, with a subtle sheen that reads as 'scientific' rather than fashionable
physical_description.texture: Uniformly smooth exterior with a barely-perceptible helix-pattern emboss that only shows under UV light. The interior is softer, slightly felted to reduce skin irritation during extended wear. Hand-worn examples develop a faint papery quality at stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Institutional white — not bright or stark, but a slightly warmed clinical white that photographs as creamy under cool lighting. The helix emboss is imperceptible without UV, making the suit read as uniformly blank-white at a distance.
physical_description.closures: Sealed magnetic snap system along center front and at hood/wrist/ankle junctures. The wrist sensor module has a small friction-fit compartment for battery replacement. Booties attach via three-point magnetic closure to prevent separation during contaminated procedures.
distinctive_features: Hood with internal structured frame designed to accommodate up to 18cm horn clearance — visible as subtle reinforcement ribs on the interior
Fin-shaped spine vents (approximately 8cm long, arranged in pairs) designed for bioluminescent skin ventilation — read as subtle anatomical accommodation
Integrated wrist-mounted contamination sensor pod with small LCD display and BCI sync indicator light
UV-visible helix emboss across entire exterior surface — anti-counterfeiting measure that glows faintly under lab lighting
Sealed magnetic closures throughout, color-matched to white with minimal visual footprint
Interior lining left unprinted, providing blank canvas for personal customization (techs often add small embroidered markers, faded writing, unofficial patches)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional/institutional — the garment's cost and sophistication place it well above survival gear, but the disposable framing and cost-cutting implementation (techs forced to reuse beyond intended lifecycle) mark it as corporate-assigned rather than individually acquired
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this suit signals: credentialed biotech worker, TESSERA employee (identifiable via branding and helix pattern), geneware-modified individual, laboratory-bound rather than field-operative. The suit is a collar in white — visible compliance, corporate tracking, institutional vulnerability. Paradoxically, the suit also reads as specialized knowledge; civilians cannot obtain a functioning version.
physical_description.condition_typical: New units are pristine and almost offensively sterile. Field-worn examples show faint creasing at elbows, knees, and spine from repeated flexing; the laminate begins to cloud slightly after 15-20 wash cycles. By cycle 25-30, small delamination cracks appear at stress points, and some techs patch with clear repair tape. Most worn examples show personalization on interior lining — embroidered initials, faded handwriting, small unofficial patches — a form of silent resistance to anonymity.

image_prompt: Fashion photography of a TESSERA BioOps lab technician coverall on a darkly-lit mannequin or model with visible geneware augmentations (bioluminescent skin patches, subtle horn protrusions, visible subdermal implant ports). Overhead lab lighting casting harsh shadows, cool blue-white clinical atmosphere. Close-up detail of the wrist contamination sensor pod glowing softly. The suit appears pristine but with subtle evidence of reuse — faint creasing, interior lining visible at neck showing personal customization marks. Dark laboratory backdrop with blurred bioreactor silhouettes. 35mm fashion editorial style, high contrast, cool color grading. --ar 2:3 --v 6
